name: Video to podcast
pitch: Convert any video file to a compact, high-quality audio file ready for podcast listening.
instructions:
Convert a video file to an audio-only version with podcast-friendly settings.

Start by asking the person which video file they want to convert and where they want the audio saved. If they do not give a path, say so and stop.

When the file path is known, check that the file exists using a shell command. If the file is not found, say so and stop.

Run a shell command to extract the audio with ffmpeg using podcast-optimized settings: aac codec, 128k bitrate, 44.1kHz sample rate, and stereo channel layout. The command should be: `ffmpeg -i "<input>" -codec:a aac -b:a 128k -ar 44100 -ac 2 "<output>.m4a"`. Replace `<input>` with the full path of the video and `<output>` with the desired audio file name without the extension.

If ffmpeg is not installed, say so and stop.

After the conversion finishes, read the new audio file to confirm it has content. If the file is empty or the command failed, say so and stop.

Offer the person the finished audio file. If they chose a save location, place the file there. If they want it in a default spot, put it in the same folder as the original video.

When nothing is found or a step fails, say plainly what could not be checked and offer to try again with different settings.

ask where to put the audio file

readme:
# Video to podcast
Convert a video file to a compact audio file with podcast-optimized settings.

**What it does:** Uses ffmpeg to extract audio at 128k bitrate, 44.1kHz sample rate, stereo, in m4a format.

**Needs:** shell_run, file_read, file_write tools. No external accounts or connectors.

**Will not:** Work if ffmpeg is not installed, or if the input file cannot be found. It will not guess file paths or overwrite existing files without asking.
